claims.text: The nanoparticles contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios.
The nanoparticles are initially crystallized as a uniform solid solution.
Slower temperature ramps combined with longer high-temperature dwells enable more atomic diffusion than faster ramps with shorter dwells.
When a thermodynamic driving force exists, the additional diffusion produced by slow ramps and long dwells causes chemical segregation.
When a thermodynamic driving force exists, the additional diffusion produced by slow ramps and long dwells causes phase separation.
Faster temperature ramps and shorter dwells help preserve the metastable solid-solution state.
Enhanced atomic diffusion at high temperature mediates the transition from a homogeneous solid solution to a chemically segregated state.
Enhanced atomic diffusion at high temperature mediates the transition from a homogeneous solid solution to a structurally segregated state.
Slow heating and extended high-temperature holds reduce kinetic trapping and allow diffusion-limited equilibration processes to manifest.
Rapid heating minimizes the time available for diffusion-driven segregation.
A 1 K/min ramp with a 60-minute dwell at 1923 K will produce more phase segregation than a 10 K/min ramp with a 10-minute dwell.
The fast-ramp, short-dwell baseline will largely preserve a single-phase solid solution.
Phase segregation can be observed as distinct compositional domains or secondary phases.
Segregation should be most pronounced during extended exposure near 1923 K with slow heating.
At significantly lower temperatures or under extremely rapid heating, diffusion may be insufficient to break down the solid solution.
The magnitude and transition threshold of segregation may depend on the elemental combination and diffusion coefficients.
The controlled comparison uses a slow-ramp, long-dwell sample and a fast-ramp, short-dwell sample at the same peak temperature.
HRTEM, EDS mapping, and XRD will be used to compare structural phases and chemical inhomogeneity between the two thermal treatments.
A lack of a significant difference in segregation or chemical inhomogeneity between the two treatments would falsify the proposed hypothesis under the specified conditions.
